extracted.intended_audience: human rights advocates and general public interested in blasphemy laws and freedom of expression
extracted.subtask_description: A news/advocacy report about a specific legal case where a stand-up comedian in India was accused of 'hurting religious sentiments', the courts' bail decisions, and calls by an NGO to uphold freedom of expression. It summarizes charges, procedural history, and the campaign position against blasphemy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to safeguard freedom of expression (Article 19 & ICCPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The End Blasphemy Laws Coalition urges the authorities to uphold its obligations to safeguard freedom of expression as prescribed by Article 19 of the Constitution of India and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities should drop investigations and prosecutions that criminalise speech, particularly where they conflict with constitutionally and internationally protected freedom of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirement for prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes police admitted that there was 'no evidence to support the case' against the comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases alleging offence to religious sentiments should be supported by actual evidence; absence of evidence undermines grounds for detention or prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds invoked (IPC sections cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints were filed alleging violations of Sections 269, 295-A, 298, 188 & 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory provisions are commonly invoked in complaints alleging public health violations, insult to religion, and public order; their use in speech-related incidents is central to assessing legality and proportionality of state action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim bail as a procedural remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim bail is described as 'a form of temporary bail that is granted while a person’s regular bail petition is pending before a court.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher courts may grant interim relief (including staying production warrants) pending fuller consideration of bail petitions; interim bail does not resolve the underlying investigation or charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event compliance and permissible grounds for complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants alleged that the group had violated COVID-19 guidance and did not have the proper permissions to hold the event, in addition to alleging hurt religious sentiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with public-health rules or permit requirements can be legitimate grounds for complaint separate from speech-related allegations; distinguishing procedural breaches from criminalisation of speech is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the comedian's style (topical/political observational comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Munawar Faruqui is described as 'known for his observational style that is typically topical and/or political.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical and political observational comedy frequently addresses sensitive societal and religious topics and may be more likely to provoke complaints or legal action; context and intent are relevant to assessing alleged offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy position: international consensus against blasphemy laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The End Blasphemy Laws campaign and Humanists International assert an international human rights consensus against 'blasphemy' laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy stance: blasphemy laws are inconsistent with international human rights standards and should be repealed or not used to criminalise expression.
